events.title: Erlang/OTP released as open source
events.summary: Ericsson released Erlang/OTP as open source on December 8, 1998 — a language built for fault-tolerant telecom switches.
events.about: Erlang uses lightweight processes, message passing, and "let it crash" supervision trees — designed for 99.999% uptime on phone switches. WhatsApp, RabbitMQ, and CouchDB used Erlang for massive concurrency. Elixir runs on the same BEAM VM with a friendlier syntax.

narrative.whyChosen: Erlang pioneered actor-model concurrency and fault tolerance decades before microservices.
narrative.whyImportant: Open-sourcing spread OTP beyond Ericsson and enabled the BEAM ecosystem (Elixir, Gleam).
narrative.problemSolved: Telecom switches needed soft real-time reliability; shared-memory threads and locks could not meet uptime requirements.
